Model-implied parameter matrices from a julia backend fit

Source: R/ctBackendSummary.R
ctBackendParMatrices.Rd

Materialise every model matrix – and the covariance and asymptotic matrices derived from them – from a raw (unconstrained) parameter vector, using the same engine code the likelihood uses.

Usage

ctBackendParMatrices(
  fit,
  raw = NULL,
  tipreds = NULL,
  state = NULL,
  filterstate = NULL,
  time = 0,
  dt = 0,
  trim = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

A ctJuliaFit, or a prepared model from ctFit(..., fit=FALSE).

raw

Raw parameter vector. Defaults to the fitted estimate.

tipreds

Time-independent predictor values for the subject to materialise. Defaults to all zero, i.e. the population values.

state

Latent state at which to evaluate state-dependent cells: one entry per latent process. Defaults to the population T0MEANS. The carrier states an intoverpop model appends hold the individually varying parameters and are not part of this – they always come from raw, so a cell reading one still varies across posterior draws when a state is supplied.

filterstate

A whole state vector as the filter carries it, carriers included, for reporting one person's matrices at a state that person's own random effects produced. Mutually exclusive with state, which is what a caller choosing an evaluation point wants.

time, dt

Time and time interval passed to state-dependent expressions that use them.

trim

Report matrices over the real latent processes (the default), as ctsem's summaries do, rather than over the augmented state an intoverpop model filters in. trim=FALSE returns the matrices the filter actually uses, carrier states included.

Value

A named list of matrices, with an attribute stateDependent giving the cells whose values are conditional on state.

Details

Internal. ctBackend* means internal throughout the package, so this is not exported; the public, backend-neutral accessor for the population matrices is ctSummaryMatrices.

For a linear model no cell depends on the state and the result is exact. For a nonlinear one, the state-dependent cells are evaluated at state and are conditional on it; attr(x, 'stateDependent') names them.

Examples

# \donttest{
# ctBackendParMatrices(fit)$DRIFT
# }
